falsification: H-C04-1: a bordered rule with random descent or an unbordered one without. H-C04-2: disagreement between observed random descent and the critical-peak test.

history.new: Exact min/max derivation lengths and the set of reachable normal forms per word from the derivation graph; random descent = all maximal derivations from each word have the same length AND the same normal form (van Oostrom); critical peaks joined by breadth-first search over exact step counts.
history.old: Exact min/max derivation lengths and the set of reachable normal forms per word from the derivation graph; critical peaks joined by breadth-first search over exact step counts.

hypothesis: H-C04-1 (bold): a terminating one-rule system has random descent iff its left-hand side is unbordered. H-C04-2: a terminating one-rule system has random descent iff each of its critical peaks (r s <- p b s -> p r for l = p b = b s) is joinable by two derivations of EQUAL length.
methodology: Exact min/max derivation lengths and the set of reachable normal forms per word from the derivation graph; random descent = all maximal derivations from each word have the same length AND the same normal form (van Oostrom); critical peaks joined by breadth-first search over exact step counts.
question: When do all maximal derivations from every word have the same length (random descent)?
